value.first: For a 2-year-old, I'd start with the chair method (camping out). She's old enough to follow you out of a bed, so closed-door timed waits don't work, but you staying put does. Get her own room set up, do the same 20-30 minute wind-down each night (bath, book, bed), and tuck her in drowsy but awake. Sit in a chair beside her bed, calm, no feeding, no rocking, just minimal touch.
value.second: Nights 1-3: chair right beside her bed. Nights 4-6: move it mid-room. Nights 7-9: by the door. Then hallway in view, then gone. Every night waking gets the same chair setup, and when she comes to your room, walk her back calmly each time. Expect protest, and expect a worse night 2 or 3. That's the old pattern breaking, not failure. The whole thing runs about 2-3 weeks.
value.third: It's working when she falls asleep faster and the chair is farther away. Pick a start week with no travel or illness, and agree with your partner first so nobody caves at 2 a.m. Snoring or gasping in sleep is worth a doctor call. I'll check in Friday. Doctors Bjorkman (a pediatrician) have a good video if you want to watch it done.
